clue.text: Loud musician not entirely cool

parts.note: F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud

indicators.note: not entirely tells us the musician word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rapper is a hip-hop musician

explanation.surface: A noisy performer who is never quite laid-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' looks like a temperament, but here it is the chilled sense of a drink served over ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes a drink served iced or chilled, so it means chilled in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Devout individual getting a long way without appropriate teachings?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the distance word goes around the teachings

parts.note: a long way means far
RI, religious instruction, is a school subject of teachings fitting a cleric

explanation.surface: A pious person travels far but lacks the proper religious grounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; RI is religious instruction, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, a pious man of faith.

clue.text: A friend overseeing motorway's initial construction

indicators.note: overseeing means sitting above, so in this down entry the friend comes on top of the motorway letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A pal supervises the early building work on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overseeing' places A and CRONY above M.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is a word built from the opening letters of a phrase.

clue.text: Some layer on ancient building

parts.note: some means part of something
a hen is a layer of eggs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A portion of something placed on top of an old structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum but is something that lays: a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the classical temple to Athena on the Athens Acropolis.

clue.text: The butt of Shakespeare's jokes?

parts.note: butt as the rear end of the body, and the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given an ass's head and laughed at

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a slang synonym for buttocks and the name of the comic weaver mocked in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Path where gold piece found

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A trail where a nugget of gold turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved course a body follows around another.

clue.text: Feeling performance during flat piece

indicators.note: during means the performance happens within the flat piece, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a tile is a thin flat piece of ceramic
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: An emotional show put on while holding a flat object.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile is the adjective for the sense of touch, so it serves for feeling as a modifier.

clue.text: Seed providing vitamin in bread and 15

indicators.note: in places the vitamin letter inside the bread word

parts.note: bread is slang for money
K is a vitamin
15-down is FRUITCAKE, a crazy person, which is also a nut

explanation.surface: A seed rich in vitamins found in bread and fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to 15-down, read as a madman: NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey nut is a peanut in its shell, the seed of the groundnut plant.

clue.text: Sign with line reading location

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A star sign paired with a line of verse being read aloud somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a place where people go to read books.

clue.text: Offensive individual pinching degree, heading for exit

indicators.note: pinching means the individual word grips the degree and letter inside it

parts.note: one is an individual
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A rude person grabs a diploma on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes E from 'exit'; ONE holds BSC plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes something indecent and repugnant.

clue.text: One taking the lead by a neck?

definitions.text: One taking the lead by a neck?

parts.words: One taking the lead by a neck?
parts.note: sounds like a narrow race win, but describes the band round a pet's neck to which a leash attaches, and also the white band a priest wears

explanation.definitionFit: A dog collar is the neckband a leash clips to, and the clerical collar of clergy.

clue.text: Garment, design of technocrat

indicators.note: design of means the letters of the next word are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing styled by a technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted military-style raincoat, an item of clothing.

clue.text: One has not quite gone for suggestion

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not quite means the word for gone loses its final letter

parts.note: gone means dead

explanation.surface: Someone almost departed offering a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last D from DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought put forward, a proposal.

clue.text: She's from the West Country

parts.note: Oman is a country in the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A lady who comes from the West Country of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' is England's southwest, but split it: W + OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A female person is referred to with this pronoun, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Corked asti left among similar stuff something to watch?

indicators.note: among places the jumbled letters inside the word for similar stuff

parts.note: Asti is a wine, so similar stuff is wine

indicators.note: corked means spoiled, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Spoiled Asti left among other wines, something to keep an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corked' scrambles ASTI and L into AISTL, which goes 'among' WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieters watch the girth of their middle, so it is a thing to keep an eye on.

clue.text: Michael acting to snort very powerful drug — this one legal

indicators.note: to snort suggests taking in, so the actor's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Michael Caine is a British actor
FF, fortissimo, is the musical abbreviation for very loud or powerful
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A famous actor snorts a potent illegal drug, though this stimulant is lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'drug' from the surface: a drug, this one legal.
explanation.definitionFit: The stimulant in coffee and tea is a lawful drug.

clue.text: One's bananas for dessert

definitions.meaning: a person who is crazy, an eccentric
a rich cake full of dried fruit

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for an eccentric, crazy person and also names a rich cake packed with dried fruit served after a meal.

clue.text: Confined by description of infection, drink untouched

indicators.note: confined by means the drink is held within the infection word

parts.note: viral describes an infection caused by a virus
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Stuck in bed with an infection, a drink is left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means pure and unspoiled, never handled.

clue.text: One shows a lot of neck finding Irish in error

definitions.text: One shows a lot of neck

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the error word

parts.note: a gaffe is an error

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky found an Irish person in a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows a lot of neck' suggests cheek, but means a long neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe has the longest neck of any animal.

clue.text: One grabbing female, appearing less than suitable

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for one holds the female letter inside it

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: A man seizing a woman, looking hardly appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means not up to standard or inappropriate.

clue.text: Mistaken if such a bloomer

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters are got wrong, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrong if one calls that a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuchsia is a flowering shrub, something that blooms.

clue.text: Use a spoon where porridge served

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, served in jail

explanation.definitionFit: The word means mix with a spoon and is also slang for jail, where a porridge sentence is served.

clue.text: Mudd awfully late admitting set-end source of income

parts.note: the setter Mudd refers to himself as me

indicators.note: admitting means the jumbled letters let the moment word in
awfully means badly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: The setter, very late, lets in a moment that pays his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of income' is the definition; the setter's name standing for ME is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal ticket is a person or thing relied on for money.

clue.text: Plant paths of hedges for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is spoken for listeners

parts.note: mazes are puzzles of paths between hedges

explanation.surface: Garden paths through hedges grown for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is a cereal crop, sweetcorn.

clue.text: Before cat gutted, standing up

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Before the cat was disembowelled, it was upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, vertical.

clue.text: Government department, one opening factory plant

indicators.note: opening means the department and numeral open up the factory word and sit inside

parts.note: a mill is a factory
FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ministry and a person open a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory too, but is the waterweed or yarrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Milfoil is yarrow or a water plant with feathery leaves.

clue.text: Animal hospital capital, though beaver evidently absent?

indicators.note: evidently absent means the beaver's structure is plainly missing from the capital

parts.note: Amsterdam is the Dutch capital
a beaver builds a dam, so the dam stands for the beaver's work

explanation.surface: A hospital in a capital city, though the beavers seem gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: Amsterdam's name ends in the very thing a beaver builds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent kept as a pet.

clue.text: English city where old film about to make comeback

parts.note: ex means former, old
ET is a Spielberg film

indicators.note: make comeback means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about

explanation.surface: A city where an old film returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county town of Devon in England.

clue.text: Go off with speed to capture record

indicators.note: to capture means the speed word holds the record inside it

parts.note: to dart is to move at speed
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Leave quickly with a stolen recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave, set out.
